newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: HEINEKEN SAYS DOUBLE DIGIT GROWTH UNSURE.
newsitem.headline: HEINEKEN SAYS DOUBLE DIGIT GROWTH UNSURE.

text.p: Dutch brewer Heineken NV said on Friday that double digit net profit growth over the next three years could not be guaranteed.

Speaking at a news conference to present first half results, chairman Karel Vuursteen said: "Within this integration phase it's very difficult to give a prediction, but over the next three years I don't think you can count on double digit net profit growth."
Vuursteen was responding to questions from journalists at the news conference, questioning the company's earlier statement that 1996 net profit would be somewhat below 1995's 664 million guilders.

He told reporters time would be necessary to integrate the distribution systems and brand portfolios of recent acquisitions in France, including the Fischer Group. Fischer was not seen contributing to net profits for around three years.

Heineken shares have long been bourse favourites, boosted by six years of double digit net profit growth and big turnover rises to an all time high of 402.00 guilders in June. -- Amsterdam Newsroom +31 20 504 5000
